# Legacy observations: T2 Position and Move (local probe, 2026-10-05)

Captured by the `legacy_position_capture` probe ([`position_capture.cpp`](../../../../tools/legacy-capture/position_capture.cpp), target in [`tools/legacy-capture/CMakeLists.txt`](../../../../tools/legacy-capture/CMakeLists.txt)) on the cases in [`inputs/position-cases.txt`](../../../../tools/legacy-capture/inputs/position-cases.txt). The probe compiles the legacy `HikariSub/VisualPosition.cpp` and `HikariSub/VisualMove.cpp` at `20d647c4` unchanged, with the legacy `Timebase.cpp`, and copies these out of their files unchanged ([`extract_functions.py`](../../../../tools/legacy-capture/extract_functions.py)): the class declarations of `Visuals`, `PosData`, `Position` and `Move` (`Visuals.h`), `FindData` and `TagFindReplace` (`TagFindReplace.h`), `TagData` and `ParseData` (`SubsDialogue.h`); `Visuals`' constructor, `SizeChanged`, both `SetVisual`s, `Draw`, `GetPosition`, `GetPosnScale`, `GetMoveTimes`, `GetDialoguesWithoutPosition`, `GetDialogueAdditionalPosition`, `GetRectFromSize`, `IsInRect`, `RenderSubs`, `SetModified`, `GetTextSize`, `GetDrawingSize`, `GetVectorPoints`, `Curve` and the wx drawing (`Visuals.cpp`); `FindTag`, `Replace`, `ChangeText`, `GetPositionInText`, `GetDouble`, `TagValueToStyle` and `FindBrackets` (`TagFindReplace.cpp`); `Dialogue::GetDefaultPosition`, `ParseTags`, `ClearParse` and `TagData`/`ParseData` (`SubsDialogue.cpp`); `Styles`' constructor, `Copy` and `Get*Double` (`styles.cpp`); `CalcMovePosition` (`UtilsWindows.cpp`); `getfloat` and `FindFromEnd` (`config.cpp`).

They run against the stand-ins in [`tools/legacy-capture/position/`](../../../../tools/legacy-capture/position): the Lines, selection, Styles and Script Info (`SubsFile`), the Grid (`SubsGrid`: `CopyDialogue`, and `SetModified` as `SubsGridBase.cpp:1125-1160` does it: a history step when a Line was copied, the editor reloaded with `redit`, and the tool set again unless `dummy`: `ShowEditOnVideo`'s `SetVisual`), the Line editor (`EditBox`: `edit->line` as a copy of the active Line, its text fields, and `Send` writing the modified field into the Line and then `SetModified(type, false, visualdummy)` as `SubsGrid::ChangeLine` does), the video (`Tell`, the `Timebase` from the case's frame starts), the D3DX line and device (`HikariSub/d3dx9.h`), and a text measure the rewrite's replay repeats (`GetLineTextExtents`: half the font size a character, 1.25 times its height, descent 0.25 and external leading 0.125 times, scaled by ScaleX/ScaleY as legacy's tail does). The Direct3D handles (`DrawRect`, `DrawCircle`, `DrawCross`, `DrawArrow` with its arithmetic, `DrawDashedLine`, `DrawWarning`) are recorded instead of drawn: the arrow by its triangle's tip and where the line now ends (`arrow`) and its base's two corners (`arrowbase`), the dashed line whole (`dashed`) and each dash its loop (`Visuals.cpp:402-423`) hands `line->Draw` (`dash`). Before each event the probe draws (`Draw`), as the render before an event would, so `blockevents` is what legacy had.

Built locally with GCC 16.2.1 and the distribution's wxWidgets 3.2.11 (wxGTK). Run:

```
cmake -S tools/legacy-capture -B <dir> -DLEGACY_SOURCE=<checkout at 20d647c4> -DWX_CONFIG=$(which wx-config)
cmake --build <dir> --target legacy_position_capture
<dir>/legacy_position_capture < tools/legacy-capture/inputs/position-cases.txt > observations.jsonl
```

`observations.jsonl` holds one line per dump (80 over 33 cases): every Line's text and translation, the history entries, the log, the tool's coefficients, Position's data (each target's position and last position in the view, its tag's place `TextPos`, whether the tag goes into a new block, its `\move` table), the rectangle, its visibility, the alignment and the active Line's alignment byte; Move's points, its times and the two points; whether events are blocked; and the recorded handles. sha256 `5176067f…22aae2`.

The cases: a plain Line dragged; twelve tag forms at once (no tag, `\pos`, a block without one, `\move` with and without times, two `\pos`, a malformed `\pos(abc,2)`, `\pos` in a later block, a comment, two blocks, margins, spaces in the values) dragged as a batch; the Shift axis lock; a right click; a double click; the A/D/W/S keys with Shift, Ctrl, Alt alone and Ctrl+Alt; the middle-click helper cross, dragged, and its drag ended by a time outside the Line's (`pos-helper-blocked`); a Line outside the video's time and a comment (blocked); TLMode; a zoomed and a pillarboxed view; "Set position by rectangle" with every alignment group and X or Y alone, on text with `\bord`, `\shad`, `\fscx` and `\N` and on a drawing; the alignment chosen without the rectangle; a `\move` on a VFR video; stacking of unpositioned Lines; another active Line with the rectangle shown; Move dragged from its start and end, by the right button, with Shift, by the keys (A/D/W/S, J/L/I/K), the middle click, a batch of four Lines, TLMode, a zoomed view, two points on CFR and VFR video, on the same frame, toggled, the helper cross, and outside the Line's time.

## Compared with the rewrite

`VisualPositionCapture.ReplaysTheLegacyProbe` (`hikari_application_visual_position_tests`) builds each case's Document, view and timebase, sets the tool from the case's toolbar value and runs its events through `visual::PositionTool` and `visual::MoveTool`; every dump's texts, history, log, positions (float for float), tag places, `\move` tables, rectangle, alignment bytes, Move points and times, blocking and handles (squares, circles, crosses, the arrows' triangles and where their lines end, the helper cross's dashes) are equal. A key in a case is its press and its release in the rewrite: legacy committed on the press, the transaction rule (#55) on the release, so the texts and steps after each key agree.

The capture shows these legacy behaviours, kept:

- A click without a drag still writes `\pos` (one step): a Line without a tag gets one at its default position (with the stacking offset), a `\move` becomes `\pos` at its start (`pos-double-click`, `pos-helper`).
- A malformed `\pos(abc,2)` stays and a new `\pos` goes first in the first block (`pos-forms`); so does `\pos( 7 , 8 )`, whose trailing spaces fail `ToCDouble`. A `\pos` in a later block is found and replaced where it is.
- Moving the helper cross commits `\pos` on the release (`SavePosition` runs before the helper check, `pos-helper`); a press within four pixels of the window's corner grabs the hidden helper. A render while none of the Lines is visible ends the helper's drag (`Position::Draw` clears `movingHelperLine`), so when the Line shows again the pointer no longer carries the cross (`pos-helper-blocked`).
- The keys nudge while the Line is outside the video's time (VideoBox hands them on, `pos-invisible`); Alt alone does nothing, Ctrl+Alt nudges.
- Choosing an alignment, with or without the rectangle, writes `\pos` into every target (`pos-align-norect`), a `\move` becoming `\pos` at its start.
- Move's editor path commits the editor's text as the last preview left it: a middle click writes nothing new but records a step (`move-middle`), and the tool is not set again after its commits, so its points stay where the drag left them.
- In a batch, a right click leaves every end where it was (`lastTo` is taken after the click moves `to`, `move-batch`).
- The two-point move uses the time of the first extrapolation for every later one (`lastVideoTime` is set once) and the `\move`'s own start, not the first point's frame (`move-two-cfr`); on the first point's frame it logs "Video must be set at least one frame after the line's start time" and writes nothing (`move-two-same-frame`).
- With the rectangle shown, making another Line active re-places it with a commit that does not set the tool again, so the next drag replaces the old tag's length in the new text (`pos-rect-other-line` writes `{\an7\pos(-16,10.5)5)}other`). A proposed departure in the T2 report; kept.
